text:
alex: quick check — planning to bump replicas for inference-api statefulset from 3 -> 5 via Terraform to handle higher tail traffic. also adding a `preStop` hook to sleep 30s and setting `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 40`. anyone see immediate problems with rollout timeouts / PVC detaches?

priya: fyi statefulset rolling update is ordinal-based. if we flip replicas from 3->5 it will create pods 3 and 4 (ok). main risk is if nodes are tight and kubelet delays attach/detach. what's the storage class? 

alex: storage class is `fast-ssd-retain`, reclaimPolicy=Retain, WaitForFirstConsumer. requests will also increase (cpu: 2000m -> 2500m, mem: 8Gi -> 10Gi). HPA is not enabled for this STS.

jamal: two quick items: (1) PDB: with replicas 5 set `minAvailable: 3` so we don't drain below capacity during node maintenance. (2) add a small rollout partition in the k8s spec so we can canary one ordinal first if we need.

lydia: +1 to canary. Also ensure `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` > sum(shutdown hooks + preStop sleep + app drain). If your app needs 25s to drain connections, GRACE=40 seems safe. Also update readinessProbe initialDelay/period so probe doesn't flake during startup.

infra-sre: node autoscaler note — bumping requests might change bin-packing and trigger scale-up. schedule the roll during low-traffic window or ensure cluster has headroom. Also increase `attach-detach-reconcile-sync` in kube-controller-manager config if you see detach slowness, but that's infra-side.

priya: terraform diff suggestion: don't change the label selectors or selectors' hash in same PR as replica bump. separate plan for selector changes. For the preStop hook, add a comment so oncall knows why it's 30s.

alex: here's the planned snippet in the TF k8s manifest (rough):
```yaml
spec:
  replicas: 5
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 4   # canary the last ordinal first
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: inference-api
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 40
      containers:
      - name: api
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "2500m"
            memory: "10Gi"
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 30; /usr/local/bin/drain-connections"]
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 10
```

jamal: that looks fine. suggestion: set partition to 4 only during the canary PR, then remove partition to resume regular rolling updates. Also add an annotation `rollout.redwood.com/initiator: alex` so we can trace.

deploy-bot: terraform plan succeeded -> link: https://ci.redwood.internal/plan/5678 (plan shows 2 new pods, resource delta +2 CPUs +4Gi RAM) :white_check_mark:

lydia: once plan is applied watch for `FailedAttachVolume` and `VolumeDetached` events. If you hit those, escalate to infra-sre immediately. Also verify kubelet logs on new nodes for attach timeouts.

alex: thanks all. I'll split selector/label changes into a follow-up, open the canary partition PR now, and run the plan in the maintenance window tomorrow 02:00 UTC. will ping here when plan/apply starts.

infra-sre: ack — we'll keep an eye on node autoscaler. ping @infra-sre if you want us to pre-warm nodes.

alex: will do. thanks :)
